## Calculations

```{r}
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# sqrt(): returns the nonnegative square root of a nonnegative number.
# set.seed(): fixes the pseudorandom sequence so rerunning the same code reproduces its artificial draws.
# replicate(): repeats an expression n times and collects the results.
# mean(): computes an average; logical TRUE/FALSE values contribute 1/0, giving a proportion.
# rnorm(): generates artificial normal draws; n is the draw count and sd is standard deviation.
# sd(): computes sample standard deviation using denominator n-1.
# Calculate design-specific SEs for the two requested sample sizes.
# The correction applies to sampling without replacement from N=2500, unlike the independent simulation.
n <- c(30,120)
knitr::kable(data.frame(n=n, fraction=n/2500, approximate=4000/sqrt(n),
 corrected=4000/sqrt(n)*sqrt((2500-n)/2499)), digits=5)
c(proportion_SE=sqrt(.6*.4/30), expected_successes=30*.6, expected_failures=30*.4)
set.seed(307312)
means <- replicate(4000,mean(rnorm(120,71800,4000)))
c(empirical_SE=sd(means), theoretical_SE=4000/sqrt(120))
```

Approximate SEs: \$730.30 and \$365.15; individual SD remains \$4,000. Fractions are .012 and .048, so neither exceeds 5%. Expected counts 18 and 12 meet our rule. A simulation using independent normal draws supports the model calculation, not an empirical claim about EAI. The CLT concerns means, and its independent-data version does not handle arbitrary coworker dependence.
